defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation entanglement at the ferrite/austenite phase boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocation entanglements occur at the phase boundary between ferrite and austenite, attributed to the inconsistent deformation of ferrite and austenite during deformation (annealed 0Cr and 6Cr strips after tensile fracture).

defect_interactions.interaction_type: slip bands crossing a low-angle grain boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Slip bands extend through a grain boundary producing many small steps at the boundary; SADPs on both sides give a low-angle grain boundary with a misorientation of 2.56°, observed only at high strain and rarely.

interfaces.interface_notes: After tensile fracture of the annealed 6Cr strip a low-angle grain boundary (misorientation 2.56°) shearable by slip bands was observed; the phenomenon occurs only at high strain and is rarely observed (reason unclear).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h promotes the δ-ferrite → ordered DO3 transformation (43.5–45.0° XRD double peak collapses to a single peak) and promotes precipitation/growth of κ-carbides in the γ-austenite; Cr addition increases δ-ferrite volume fraction and DO3 content while decreasing κ-carbide precipitation.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip bands (with dislocation arrays) form in the γ-austenite at the early strain stage; slip bands can extend through a grain boundary. {111} planar slip bands were observed in cold-rolled austenite, and both slip bands and microbands appear during deformation.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength increase on annealing (600 °C, 3 h)
ultimate tensile strength and yield strength; Cr addition decreases YS but after annealing Cr-containing strips show higher UTS
comparative_performance.value: Annealed 6Cr UTS 1028 MPa > annealed 0Cr UTS 1016 MPa; annealed 6Cr YS 859 MPa < annealed 0Cr YS 967 MPa

processing_steps.method: cold-crucible levitation melting, then induction remelting
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot was prepared by melting 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite by a cold-crucible levitation melting setup; the metal ingot was remelted by induction melting.
Molten metal was poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm under an argon atmosphere; as-cast steel strips with size 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm were obtained.

Some as-cast steel strips were annealed at 600 °C for 3 h in a tubular vacuum furnace, referred to as 'annealed steel strips'; annealing at 600 °C for 3 h promotes the precipitation of κ-carbides without coarsening.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times on an MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester; specimens machined from the steel strips.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm

strain_hardening_rate.value: The strain hardening rate of the annealed 6Cr strip is lower than that of the corresponding as-cast strip and decreases monotonically during deformation (no stable plateau).

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of the annealed 6Cr strip (Fig. 3b) rises gradually past 1000 MPa, extending furthest (to ~32–36% strain) among the annealed strips; true stress–strain and strain hardening rate curves shown in Fig. 3(d).

precipitates.coherency: Ordered κ-carbides give superlattice reflections in the [110] SADP, orientation relationship [110]γ // [110]κ.
precipitates.distribution: Nano-scale; the volume fraction/size of κ-carbides decrease with Cr addition; in the annealed 6Cr strip the (001) dark-field image is essentially featureless (no resolvable κ-carbide particles), indicating a very small number/size.

precipitates.coherency: DO3 ordering confirmed by superlattice reflections; DO3 is a body-centered cubic crystal with lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm (Fm3m, Fe/Mn at corners, Al at alternate centers).
precipitates.distribution: Nano-scale ordered phase precipitated within the δ-ferrite (dense nanoscale speckles in the (00-2) dark-field image).

microstructure_list.region: δ-ferrite islands distributed in the γ-austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: Annealed near-rapidly solidified low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-6Cr steel strip consists of a γ-austenite matrix containing a small amount of nano-scale κ-carbides, with irregularly shaped, blocky and interconnected δ-ferrite distributed evenly in the matrix; the δ-ferrite contains an ordered DO3 phase. XRD confirms γ-austenite, δ-ferrite and ordered DO3; upon annealing the 43.5–45.0° double peak of the as-cast strip becomes essentially a single peak whose relative intensity increases with Cr content, indicating increased ordered DO3 content.

unmapped_findings: Measured composition of the annealed 6Cr strip (Table 1, wt.%): Mn 20.18, Al 9.12, C 1.20, Cr 6.08, S 0.0011, Fe Bal.
UTS × TE product for the annealed 6Cr strip is 32.9 GPa %.
Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h increases the yield strength of the 6Cr strip by 141 MPa (from 718 MPa as-cast to 859 MPa annealed).
The annealed 6Cr steel strip fractured at a true strain of 0.298 during tensile testing.

Nano-scale κ-carbides were too small/numerous to be resolved in the (001) dark-field TEM image of the annealed 6Cr strip (near-featureless DF), consistent with the Cr-driven reduction of κ-carbide precipitation; the paper quantifies κ-carbides only for annealed 0Cr (7%, 8 nm) and 3Cr (4%, 4 nm).
Lattice parameters reported for the as-cast 6Cr strip: κ-carbide 0.389 nm and γ-austenite 0.384 nm (as-cast, not the annealed condition).

A double (slip-band and microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening of the low-density steel strips: slip bands act at the early strain stage and microbands at the final strain stage; the number of nano-scale κ-carbides plays a crucial role in the strain hardening rate at the early strain stage.
